summary: Georgian Bay's first light, 1858: a limestone tower on Gig Point, a keeper marooned in 1946, and a heritage association that has pressed for its restoration.

lens.note: The original Fresnel lens still shows the white flash (LighthouseFriends)

structures.type: tapered cylindrical stone tower with balcony and lantern

access.note: Reached only by boat. Site open and tower closed (Lighthouse Directory); LighthouseFriends says grounds and tower closed.

facts.agency: Canadian Coast Guard (owner); Parks Canada, Fathom Five National Marine Park (site manager, per the Lighthouse Directory)

events.note: Limestone tower built under contractor John Brown, begun in the summer of 1855; stonework completed in 1857
Second-order Fresnel lens lit by Keeper George Collins on 30 October 1858
Steam fog alarm added in a building northwest of the lighthouse
Steam fog horn replaced by a diaphone operated by compressed air
Original fog-alarm building destroyed by fire; current foghorn building built October and November 1948
Cove Island Lightstation Heritage Association formed; memorandum of understanding with the Coast Guard to restore the station
A $200,000 restoration announced, including repairs to the keeper's house and repainting the tower (announced; completion not confirmed in sources read)

notes_for_editor: Most of the station history comes from LighthouseFriends (copyrighted: facts paraphrased; short quotations used in the evidence only). The 1850s-1870s departmental reports are not in the local corpus (marine_ca starts with the year to June 1900), so the Collins, McBeath and Rescue episodes rest on LighthouseFriends alone. The 1912 keepers' table (Cove Island, Kenneth McLeod) is an OCR table read by row; the date beside McLeod is garbled and not used. Keepers William Spears (1949-76), Robert Nelder (1977-81) and Jack Vaughan (1982-91) served after 1960; they are named only as LighthouseFriends names them, with no personal detail beyond its keeper list. Iris Banas is included as a family member who kept the light dark in 1946. Disagreements: focal height 31.8 m (LighthouseFriends) against 31.4 m (station record, CCG list); range 16 M (LighthouseFriends) against 11 nm (station record); characteristic Fl W 5s (LighthouseFriends, Wikipedia lead) against Fl W 10s (station record from the CCG list); tower 80 ft (24.4 m) to full height in October 1856 (LighthouseFriends) against 28.4 m (LighthouseFriends table) and 24 m (Wikipedia lead). The Lighthouse Directory says the site is open and the tower closed; LighthouseFriends says the grounds are closed too. Check before a visit. The Directory's 2015 restoration is an announcement; completion not found. The station record's 1991 heritage designation is not confirmed by any source read here. The Morrow's 1923 grounding is reported to the 'Tobermory station' as in the Big Tub entry; the report does not say which light that was. The 1912 keepers' table row 'Cove Island, Kenneth McLeod' is OCR; matched by row. The story uses 'eighty feet' (24.4 m) from LighthouseFriends for the 1856 full height; the station record's 28.4 m and Wikipedia's 24 m are not reconciled. Ranges are given as 16 miles in LighthouseFriends' table (no unit stated); the story does not give a range. FACT-CHECK 2026-10-27: every footnoted sentence was checked against the cached LighthouseFriends page, the Lighthouse Directory and the Canadian Register entry, and the corpus page of each Marine report (Turret Chief p.229, Morrow p.148, Cove diaphone p.40, McLeod table p.247 confirmed by the OCR page index). Changes to the story: the 1856 tower height is now stated as disputed (LighthouseFriends' text 80 ft, 24.4 m; its data table 28.4 m above ground; the Directory 24 m). The Morrow's release is dated 16 May (the report gives it; the earlier draft left the date out). The 1946 boat is given in metres first (6.1 m (20 ft)). The 'bad winter' was not in any source (the source describes a family without provisions in early December 1860 with the lake beginning to freeze), so the phrase was removed. Two sentences that had no footnote now carry [^7] (ownership and the site status in the Directory). The 2015 restoration is still shown as announced; no completion is recorded in the sources read, and the story says so. OCR matched by row: the 1912 keepers' table line 'Cove Island , Kenneth McLeod June l'.t. 11103' is one OCR line (station, keeper and appointment on the same row); the appointment date is garbled and is not used. Living-person rule: William Spears (1949-76), Robert Nelder (1977-81) and Jack Vaughan (1982-91) are named only as LighthouseFriends names them, with their public role (weather reports, rescues, head keeper's caretaking) and no personal detail. Paraphrases that followed LighthouseFriends too closely (contractor's craft, caretaker, icy water, the Rescue's raft) were rewritten.
